node.title: Re: Converting dates with Date:Format
node.author: 1nickt
node.doctext:
For completeness: [mod://DateTime]:

(Note that your input has no timezone info, so you can't use %Z to print the timezone with accuracy. Also note that you have two spaces in your input, so the solution reflects that.) use DateTime::Format::Strptime; my $formatter = DateTime::Format::Strptime->new(pattern => "%F %T"); my $dt_obj = $formatter->parse_datetime("2008-11-03 19:03:44"); my $datetime = $dt_obj->strftime("%a, %d %b %Y %T EST"); Or, more succinctly as a one-liner: perl -ML -E'say DateTime::Format::Strptime->new(pattern => "%F %T")-> parse_datetime("2008-11-03 19:03:44")->strftime("%a, %d %b %Y %T EST"); ' Output: Mon, 03 Nov 2008 19:03:44 EST

Hope this helps!


The way forward always starts with a minimal test.
